UAE Oil Production Nears Record After OPEC Exit

The United Arab Emirates pumped roughly 3.8 million barrels per day in June, the highest monthly figure recorded since the country began publishing production data, as the producer moved past the quota discipline that had constrained its output for years.

The increase followed the formal exit from the OPEC production agreement on May 1, a decision that freed ADNOC to bring idle capacity back online far faster than analysts covering the Gulf had expected at the start of the year.

Traders said the additional barrels arrived while Brent hovered near 72 dollars, and that the extra supply helped cap a rally that had been building on the back of refinery outages in Asia during the second quarter of the year.
